lines: The besties read Anthropic's S-1 as evidence of an unusually capital-efficient business, with explosive revenue growth and a founder-controlled structure (50.1% voting power on a single share class) that they say could make it one of the biggest venture outcomes ever.

They highlight roughly $100 billion in cash reserves despite spending only a small share of capital raised, and claim recursive self-improvement yields 'compute multipliers' that let Anthropic cut token prices while widening gross margins.

Falling token costs, they argue, are triggering a Jevons Paradox of surging consumption, while data center capacity and power have become the binding constraint and AI's capital needs now rival US Treasury issuance, a new systemic risk.

On Google's roughly $500 billion one-day market-cap drop, the hosts see slowing core search ads as a sign AI answers are structurally disrupting click-based search; the episode closes with midterm election predictions.
title: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google’s $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
